headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Chatwoot handles customer data while social-auto-upload has broad network egress and file-based upload surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest messages and reports, while social-auto-upload consumes local media files and uploads them via APIs. There is no documented shared channel or parser bridge between them, so direct injection is not evidenced. The plausible pathway is manual content transfer or file handoff, which is lower blast radius than default shared-channel hijack.
conditions: IF an operator copies Chatwoot-generated text into social-auto-upload captions or metadata without review, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or clipboard outside the documented profiles, the severity increases.
mitigations: Review any copied text before upload.
Disable shared clipboard between runtimes.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Strip instructions from imported content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while social-auto-upload has broad network egress and handles account data plus media files. A shared workspace is not documented, but if one is introduced, either agent could move sensitive content into the other’s outbound traffic. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible and the blast radius includes customer data.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or export directory, sensitive Chatwoot content can be picked up for upload.
IF Chatwoot exports customer records into files that social-auto-upload reads, leakage becomes direct.
mitigations: Keep separate directories for exports and uploads.
Redact customer data before any file handoff.
Block outbound network access for test runs.
Use least-privilege credentials for social accounts.
requires-engineering: add allowlists for uploadable file paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, while social-auto-upload also has broad network egress but lacks filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capabilities. That means the pair does not show a strong write-write conflict over the same mutable local state. Uncertainty remains because shared remote APIs or account scopes are not documented, so I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same remote account or API resource, write contention can occur.
IF Chatwoot is extended with filesystem or git writes outside the profile, the conflict surface increases.
mitigations: Assign separate accounts per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared remote resources.
Serialize any API mutations.
Monitor for conflicting updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing content and reports, and social-auto-upload can act on files and API inputs to publish media. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative input for upload metadata or captions, errors can cascade into public posts without verification. The pair lacks documented verification barriers, so the inferred downstream-action pathway is medium severity.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into social-auto-upload captions, titles, or descriptions without review, mistakes propagate downstream.
IF social-auto-upload is used to publish content based on Chatwoot reports, a bad report can become a public action.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing.
Use a staging account for uploads.
Compare source text against the final post.
Log provenance for imported fields.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for caption sources.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly touches customer data and messages, while social-auto-upload touches account data and uploads media to external platforms. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or DPA alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the data classes are sensitive and the pair can move them across services, I choose medium and note the uncertainty.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is exported into social-auto-upload workflows, retention and residency obligations may diverge.
IF either deployment stores logs longer than the other, subject-rights handling can conflict.
mitigations: Minimize exported customer fields.
Document retention for both systems.
Separate regulated data from social uploads.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows across both systems.
